version: The Tale of the Tang Tripitaka's Pilgrimage for Scriptures
feature: The earliest extant Journey-to-the-West story: the embryonic Tripitaka pilgrimage, the first appearance of the Monkey Pilgrim, and the Deep-Sand Spirit (prototype of Sha Wujing)

version: Journey to the West Zaju (Variety Play)
feature: Dramatization of the Journey story: Zhu Bajie first takes shape; Red Boy, Princess Iron Fan, and the Women's Kingdom appear

version: Journey to the West Pinghua (Plain Tale)
feature: Lost; known only from the 'Wei Zheng Beheads the Dragon' fragment in the Yongle Encyclopedia and citations in the Korean Pak T'ongsa ŏnhae

version: Shidetang Edition of Journey to the West
feature: The earliest complete hundred-chapter edition; inscribed 'collated by the Master of Huayang Cavern-Heaven'; lays the textual foundation of Journey to the West
missing_elements: Tang Sanzang's origin story (chs. 9–12 added in Qing editions)

version: Yang Minzhai Edition of Journey to the West
feature: An early reprint of the Shidetang edition with minor textual differences

version: Zhu Dingchen's Edition of the Tang Tripitaka's Westward Deliverance
feature: An abridged edition that adds Tang Sanzang's origin story (Chen Guangrui · Jiangliu'er)

version: Journey to the West: The Book of Realizing the Way (Zhengdao shu)
year: Qing Kangxi · 1663 · annotated by Wang Xiangxu
feature: First to interpret the Journey through 'Realization of the Way'; inserts Tang Sanzang's origin story as Chapter 9; attributes the commentary to Qiu Chuji
key_role_introduction: Tang Sanzang's origin entering the main text

version: The True Interpretation of the Journey West (Xiyou zhenquan)
year: Qing Kangxi · 1696 · annotated by Chen Shibin
feature: Annotated by Chen Shibin; interprets the Journey through the Golden Elixir; the most popular Qing commentary edition

version: New Commentary on Journey to the West (Xinshuo)
year: Qing Qianlong · 1753 · annotated by Zhang Shushen
feature: Annotated by Zhang Shushen; interprets the Journey through Confucianism; argues that the Great Learning, Doctrine of the Mean, and Analects are its inner doctrine

version: The Original Intent of the Journey West (Xiyou yuanzhi)
year: Qing Qianlong · 1753 · annotated by Liu Yiming
feature: Annotated by Liu Yiming of the Daoist Longmen lineage; the most systematic Neidan (inner-alchemy) interpretation of the Journey
